name: MC78M05BDTRKG
title: MC78M00, MC78M00A, NCV78M00 series: 500 mA positive fixed voltage regulators
summary: A family of three-terminal positive linear regulators with fixed outputs from 5 V to 24 V and up to 500 mA with enough heat sinking: the half-current version of the MC7800. Current limiting, thermal shutdown and safe-area protection of the pass transistor are built in, and no external parts are required. B and AB grades are specified from −40 °C, C and AC from 0 °C; the A grades hold the output to ±2 %. The MC78M05BDTRKG is the 5.0 V B-grade part in DPAK-3 on tape and reel.
key_figures: 500 mA max with heat sinking; 700 mA peak typ
35 Vdc max (5.0 V to 18 V parts)
80 dB typ at 120 Hz, IO = 300 mA

notes: DT suffix: DPAK-3 (case 369C); T suffix: TO-220 (case 221AB). The MC78M00A parts hold the output to ±2 %.
NCV parts (marked *) are specified from −40 °C to +125 °C, guaranteed by design, AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable, for automotive and other uses that need site and change control.
The A grade (±2 %) is offered at 5.0, 8.0, 12 and 15 V.
DPAK marking: xxxxxG over ALYWW; TO-220 marking: MC 78MxxXXT over AWLYWWG. xx is the voltage, XX the suffix, A assembly location, WL or L wafer lot, Y year, WW work week, G Pb-free.

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: A constant-current source into a load returned to ground. The regulator holds its 5.0 V output across R, and the regulator's ground pin returns to the far end of R, so the load sees the R current plus the regulator's own bias current. The 5 V part keeps the dissipation down. A 0.33 µF capacitor bypasses the input.

parts.note: sets the current; 10 Ω, 10 W gives 500 mA

notes: Output compliance runs up to the input voltage less 7.0 V.

circuits.title: Adjustable output regulator
circuits.description: An MC1741 op amp drives the regulator's ground pin so the output can be set above 5 V. The op amp is wired as a follower (output back to its inverting input) and its non-inverting input takes the wiper of a 10 kΩ potentiometer across the output; a 1.0 kΩ resistor loads the ground-pin node to ground. The op amp runs from the regulator's input. Output range 7.0 V to 20 V, with at least 2.0 V from input to output.

parts.note: potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 the ends, W the wiper

notes: MC1741 pins: 2 inverting input (IN-), 3 non-inverting input (IN+), 4 V-, 6 output, 7 V+.
The lowest output this arrangement reaches is 2.0 V above the regulator's own voltage.

circuits.title: Current boost regulator
circuits.description: An MJ2955 PNP pass transistor in parallel with the regulator carries the extra current, up to 5.0 A. R, with the PNP's base-emitter voltage, sets where the transistor starts to conduct. 1.0 µF capacitors sit at the regulator's input and output. XX stands for the two digits of the output voltage.

parts.note: sets, with the VBE of Q1, where Q1 starts to conduct

notes: The circuit has no short-circuit protection.
The minimum input-output voltage rises by the VBE of the pass transistor.

circuits.title: Current boost with short circuit protection
circuits.description: The current boost circuit with a short-circuit limit added: a sense resistor RSC in the MJ2955's emitter and a 2N6049 PNP across it. When the drop on RSC turns the 2N6049 on, it pulls the MJ2955's base toward its emitter and limits the boost current. A 1.0 µF capacitor sits at the regulator's input. XX stands for the two digits of the output voltage.

parts.note: or equivalent; 4.0 A plastic power transistor

notes: The sensing PNP has to carry the regulator's own short-circuit current, hence the 4.0 A part.

operation.text: Electrically the MC7800 series at half the rated output current, for regulating a supply locally on a card. Fixed outputs of 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20 and 24 V. The inside holds 28 active transistors.

Three protections are built in: thermal overload shuts the regulator down under excess dissipation; short-circuit limiting caps the output current; safe-area compensation lets less current through as more voltage sits on the pass transistor, so peak output current falls with input-output voltage.

Low-current designs often work without compensation capacitors. When the supply filter is a long run of wire away, or the load capacitance is large, the input wants a bypass capacitor of 0.33 µF or more with low impedance at high frequency (tantalum, mylar or similar), on short leads right at the input and ground pins, for stability under every load.
There is no remote sense lead, so ground loops and voltage drops in the leads appear in the output; keep them small. The heat-sink tab is joined to pin 2 (ground).

θJA is 70 °C/W for TO-220 and 92 °C/W for DPAK, θJC 5.0 °C/W for both. On a board, the DPAK's θJA falls with the length of the square of 2.0 oz copper under it (from 0 to 30 mm), and the dissipation allowed at 50 °C ambient rises with it. Power dissipation is limited inside the part.
Electrical figures hold from Tlow to Thigh: 0 °C to +125 °C junction for the C and AC grades, −40 °C to +125 °C for B, AB and the NCV parts.

Line regulation: output change for an input change, measured at low dissipation or with pulses so the chip temperature barely moves. Load regulation: output change for a load change at constant chip temperature. Maximum power dissipation: the highest total dissipation at which the specifications hold. Input bias current: the part of the input current that does not reach the load. Output noise voltage: rms AC output over a stated band, with a constant load and no input ripple. Long-term stability: output stability under accelerated life testing at the maximum rated voltage and dissipation.
A resistor from OUT to the GND pin, with the load hung from the GND pin, turns the part into a current source. The 5 V part keeps dissipation down; the load can rise to the input voltage less 7.0 V.
An op amp driving the GND pin sets higher or intermediate outputs while keeping the regulation; the output cannot go below 2.0 V above the regulator's own voltage.

An MJ2955 PNP across the regulator carries up to 5.0 A; R and the PNP's VBE set where it starts to conduct, the circuit is not short-circuit proof and the minimum input-output voltage rises by one VBE. A sense resistor RSC and a second PNP add short-circuit protection; that PNP must handle the regulator's short-circuit current, so a 4.0 A plastic power transistor is used.
